106	
107	#### Monomorphisms and epimorphisms
108	
109	A **monomorphism** is an injective homomorphism and an **epimorphism** is a
110	surjective one.  Each comes in the two forms `hom`{.AgdaFunction} does:
111	
112	+  the predicates `IsMon`{.AgdaRecord} and `IsEpi`{.AgdaRecord}, whose fields pair
113	   the homomorphism property with `IsInjective`{.AgdaFunction} or
114	   `IsSurjective`{.AgdaFunction};
115	+  the bundled types `mon`{.AgdaFunction} and `epi`{.AgdaFunction}, which pair a
116	   setoid function with such a proof.
117	
118	Both predicates export a `HomReduct`{.AgdaFunction} that forgets the extra
119	condition, and `mon→hom`{.AgdaFunction} and `epi→hom`{.AgdaFunction} apply it to
120	the bundled forms.
121	
122	`mon→intohom`{.AgdaFunction} and `epi→ontohom`{.AgdaFunction} regroup the same
123	data the other way, as a `hom`{.AgdaFunction} paired with the injectivity or the
124	surjectivity of its underlying map.  That regrouping earns a name because the two
125	resulting types are, by definition, `_IsSubalgebraOf_`{.AgdaFunction} of
126	[Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic][] and `_IsHomImageOf_`{.AgdaFunction} of
127	[Setoid.Homomorphisms.HomomorphicImages][]; so these are the functions that turn a
128	monomorphism into a subalgebra and an epimorphism into a homomorphic image.
129	
130	```agda
131	  record IsMon (h : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]) : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ) where
132	    field
133	      isHom : IsHom h
134	      isInjective : IsInjective h
135	
136	    HomReduct : hom
137	    HomReduct = h , isHom
138	
139	  mon : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
140	  mon = Σ (𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]) IsMon
141	
142	  mon→hom : mon → hom
143	  mon→hom h = IsMon.HomReduct (proj₂ h)
144	
145	  record IsEpi (h : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]) : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ) where
146	    field
147	      isHom : IsHom h
148	      isSurjective : IsSurjective h
149	
150	    HomReduct : hom
151	    HomReduct = h , isHom
152	
153	  epi : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
154	  epi = Σ (𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]) IsEpi
155	
156	  epi→hom : epi → hom
157	  epi→hom h = IsEpi.HomReduct (proj₂ h)
158	
159	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)(𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ) where
160	  open IsEpi
161	  open IsMon
162	
163	  mon→intohom : mon 𝑨 𝑩 → Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑨 𝑩 ] IsInjective (proj₁ h)
164	  mon→intohom (hh , hhM) = (hh , isHom hhM) , isInjective hhM
165	
166	  epi→ontohom : epi 𝑨 𝑩 → Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑨 𝑩 ] IsSurjective (proj₁ h)
167	  epi→ontohom (hh , hhE) = (hh , isHom hhE) , isSurjective hhE
168	```
169	
170	Finally, we define the identity homomorphism for setoid algebras.
171	
172	```agda
173	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} where
174	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]   using ( reflexive )
175	
176	  𝒾𝒹 :  hom 𝑨 𝑨
177	  𝒾𝒹 = 𝑖𝑑 , mkIsHom (reflexive refl)
178	```

7	
8	#### Kernels of Homomorphisms
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Kernels][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	The **kernel** of a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` is the binary relation on the
13	carrier of `𝑨` that relates `a₀` and `a₁` when `h a₀` and `h a₁` are equal in `𝑩`.
14	
15	It is an equivalence relation because it is the pullback of one along `h`, which is
16	`kerRelOfEquiv`{.AgdaFunction} of [Overture.Relations][]; what this module adds is
17	that it is also compatible with the basic operations, hence a congruence, so that
18	the quotient by the kernel is again an algebra.
19	
20	`HomKerComp`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility proof, `kercon`{.AgdaFunction} is
21	the congruence, and `kerquo`{.AgdaFunction}, also written `ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h`, is the
22	quotient.
23	
24	This module also supplies the homomorphisms that go with a quotient:
25	
26	+  `πepi`{.AgdaFunction} is the canonical projection of `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ`, for any
27	   congruence `θ`, presented as an epimorphism;
28	+  `πhom`{.AgdaFunction} is its homomorphism reduct;
29	+  `πker`{.AgdaFunction} is the special case that projects onto a kernel quotient;
30	+  `ker-in-con`{.AgdaFunction} says the kernel of `πhom θ` is contained in `θ`.
31	
32	Together with the congruences of [Setoid.Congruences][], these are the components
33	with which the first homomorphism theorem of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Noether][] is
34	stated.
35

61	
62	```agda
63	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} ((hmap , hhom) : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
64	  open Algebra 𝑩   using ( Interp ) renaming ( Domain to B )
65	  open Setoid B    using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans ; isEquivalence )
66	  private h = _⟨$⟩_ hmap
67	```
68	
69	`HomKerComp` asserts that the kernel of a homomorphism is compatible with the basic operations.
70	That is, if each `(u i, v i)` belongs to the kernel, then so does the pair `((f ^ 𝑨) u , (f ^ 𝑨) v)`.
71	
72	```agda
73	  HomKerComp : 𝑨 ∣≈ kerRel _≈_ h
74	  HomKerComp f {u}{v} kuv = Goal
75	    where
76	    fhuv : (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ v)
77	    fhuv = cong Interp (refl , kuv)
78	
79	    lem1 : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ (f ^ 𝑩)(h ∘ u)
80	    lem1 = IsHom.compatible hhom
81	
82	    lem2 : (f ^ 𝑩) (h ∘ v) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
83	    lem2 = sym (IsHom.compatible hhom)
84	
85	    Goal : h ((f ^ 𝑨) u) ≈ h ((f ^ 𝑨) v)
86	    Goal = trans lem1 (trans fhuv lem2)
87	```
88	
89	The kernel of a homomorphism is a congruence of the domain, which we construct as follows.
90	
91	```agda
92	  kercon : Con 𝑨 ρᵇ
93	  kercon =  kerRel _≈_ h ,
94	            mkcon (λ x → cong hmap x)(kerRelOfEquiv isEquivalence h)(HomKerComp)
95	```
96	
97	Now that we have a congruence, we can construct the quotient relative to the kernel.
98	
99	```agda
100	  kerquo : Algebra α ρᵇ
101	  kerquo = 𝑨 ╱ kercon
102	
103	ker[_⇒_]_ :  {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) (𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ) → hom 𝑨 𝑩 → Algebra _ _
104	ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h = kerquo h
105	```
106	
107	
108	#### The canonical projection
109	
110	Given an algebra `𝑨` and a congruence `θ`, the *canonical projection* is a map
111	from `𝑨` onto `𝑨 ╱ θ` that is constructed, and proved epimorphic, as follows.
112	
113	```agda
114	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} (h : hom 𝑨 𝑩) where
115	  open IsCongruence
116	
117	  πepi : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → epi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
118	  πepi θ = p , pepi
119	    where
120	
121	    open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]    using () renaming ( sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl )
122	    open IsHom {𝑨 = (𝑨 ╱ θ)}  using ( compatible )
123	    open IsEpi
124	
125	    p : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑨 ╱ θ ]
126	    p ⟨$⟩ x = x
127	    p .cong = reflexive (θ .proj₂)
128	
129	    pepi : IsEpi 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) p
130	    pepi .isHom .compatible = ≈sym (𝒾𝒹 .proj₂ .compatible)
131	    pepi .isSurjective {y} = Image_∋_.eq y ≈refl
132	```
133	
134	In may happen that we don't care about the surjectivity of `πepi`, in which
135	case would might prefer to work with the *homomorphic reduct* of `πepi`.
136	This is obtained by applying `epi-to-hom`, like so.
137	
138	```agda
139	  πhom : (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ)
140	  πhom θ = epi→hom 𝑨 (𝑨 ╱ θ) (πepi θ)
141	```
142	
143	We combine the foregoing to define a function that takes 𝑆-algebras `𝑨` and `𝑩`,
144	and a homomorphism `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` and returns the canonical epimorphism from `𝑨`
145	onto `𝑨 [ 𝑩 ]/ker h`. (Recall, the latter is the special notation we defined
146	above for the quotient of `𝑨` modulo the kernel of `h`.)
147	
148	```agda
149	  πker : epi 𝑨 (ker[ 𝑨 ⇒ 𝑩 ] h)
150	  πker = πepi (kercon h)
151	```
152	
153	The kernel of the canonical projection of `𝑨` onto `𝑨 / θ` is equal to `θ`,
154	but since equality of inhabitants of certain types (like `Congruence` or `Rel`)
155	can be a tricky business, we settle for proving the containment `𝑨 / θ ⊆ θ`.
156	Of the two containments, this is the easier one to prove; luckily it is also
157	the one we need later.
158	
159	```agda
160	  ker-in-con : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → ∀ {x}{y} → kercon (πhom θ) .proj₁ x y →  θ .proj₁ x y
161	  ker-in-con = id
162	```

7	
8	#### Properties of Homomorphisms of Algebras
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Properties][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	This module collects some of the facts that follow from the definition of a
13	homomorphism alone, before any theory.  These include the following:
14	
15	+  homomorphisms and epimorphisms compose;
16	+  if a relation `R` is contained in the kernel of a homomorphism, then the
17	   congruence generated by `R` is also contained in the kernel;
18	+  the universe liftings and lowerings of an algebra are homomorphisms, and
19	   surjective in the lifting direction.
20	
21	The lifting results are the ones we use most.  Agda's universes are not
22	cumulative, so an algebra defined at one universe level cannot be used directly at
23	a higher universe level.  `Lift-Alg`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]
24	lifts an algebra to a higher level, and the homomorphisms defined here
25	(`ToLift`{.AgdaFunction}, `FromLift`{.AgdaFunction}, `Lift-hom`{.AgdaFunction} and
26	their one-sided variants) are what prove this lift harmless.
27	[Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][] assembles these facts into
28	`Lift-≅`{.AgdaFunction}, and the closure operators of [Setoid.Varieties.Closure][]
29	rely on them at every change of level.
30

61	
62	##### Composition of homs
63	
64	The composite of two homomorphisms is a homomorphism, and the composite of two
65	epimorphisms is an epimorphism.
66	
67	+  `⊙-is-hom`{.AgdaFunction} is the predicate form: from `IsHom 𝑨 𝑩 g` and `IsHom
68	   𝑩 𝑪 h` it proves `IsHom 𝑨 𝑪 (h ⊙ g)`, by transitivity through two steps, first
69	   pushing `g`'s compatibility across `h` with `cong h`, then applying `h`'s own
70	   compatibility.
71	+  `⊙-is-epi`{.AgdaFunction} adds surjectivity of the composite, which is
72	   `⊙-IsSurjective`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Functions.Surjective][].
73	+  `⊙-hom`{.AgdaFunction} and `⊙-epi`{.AgdaFunction} are the bundled forms.
74	
75	All four take their arguments in *diagrammatic* order, the map out of `𝑨` first
76	and the map out of `𝑩` second, although the underlying composition
77	`_⊙_`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Functions.Basic][] is written right to left; so
78	`⊙-hom f g` is read as "apply `f`, then `g`".
79	
80	```agda
81	module _
82	  {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}
83	  {𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ}
84	  {𝑪 : Algebra γ ρᶜ}
85	  where
86	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] renaming ( _≈_ to _≈₁_ ) using ()
87	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑪 ] renaming ( _≈_ to _≈₃_ ) using ( trans )
88	  open IsHom
89	  open IsEpi
90	
91	  -- The composition of homomorphisms is again a homomorphism
92	  ⊙-is-hom : {g : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]} {h : 𝔻[ 𝑩 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑪 ]}
93	    → IsHom 𝑨 𝑩 g → IsHom 𝑩 𝑪 h → IsHom 𝑨 𝑪 (h ⊙ g)
94	  ⊙-is-hom {g} {h} ghom hhom .compatible {f}{a} = trans lemg lemh
95	    where
96	    lemg : h ⟨$⟩ (g ⟨$⟩ (f ^ 𝑨) a) ≈₃ h ⟨$⟩ (f ^ 𝑩) λ x → g ⟨$⟩ a x
97	    lemg = cong h (compatible ghom)
98	
99	    lemh : h ⟨$⟩ ((f ^ 𝑩) λ x → g ⟨$⟩ a x) ≈₃ (f ^ 𝑪) λ x → h ⟨$⟩ (g ⟨$⟩ a x)
100	    lemh = compatible hhom
101	
102	  ⊙-hom : hom 𝑨 𝑩 → hom 𝑩 𝑪  → hom 𝑨 𝑪
103	  ⊙-hom (h , hhom) (g , ghom) = g ⊙ h , ⊙-is-hom hhom ghom
104	
105	  -- The composition of epimorphisms is again an epimorphism
106	  ⊙-is-epi : {g : 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]} {h : 𝔻[ 𝑩 ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝑪 ]}
107	    → IsEpi 𝑨 𝑩 g → IsEpi 𝑩 𝑪 h → IsEpi 𝑨 𝑪 (h ⊙ g)
108	  ⊙-is-epi gE hE .isHom = ⊙-is-hom (isHom gE) (isHom hE)
109	  ⊙-is-epi gE hE .isSurjective = ⊙-IsSurjective (isSurjective gE) (isSurjective hE)
110	
111	  ⊙-epi : epi 𝑨 𝑩 → epi 𝑩 𝑪  → epi 𝑨 𝑪
112	  ⊙-epi (h , hepi) (g , gepi) = g ⊙ h , ⊙-is-epi hepi gepi
113	```
114	
115	#### A kernel that collapses `R` contains the congruence generated by `R`
116	
117	If a relation `R` is contained in the kernel of a homomorphism `h` (i.e., `h`
118	collapses every `R`-pair), then the congruence `Cg R` generated by `R` is also
119	contained in that kernel.  This is exactly `Cg-least`{.AgdaFunction} applied to
120	the kernel congruence `kercon h`{.AgdaFunction}: the kernel is a congruence above
121	`R`, hence above the least such, `Cg R`.
122	
123	```agda
124	Cg⊆ker : {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} {𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ}
125	  (h : hom 𝑨 𝑩) {R : BinaryRel 𝕌[ 𝑨 ] ℓ}
126	  → R ⊆ proj₁ (kercon h) → Gen R ⊆ proj₁ (kercon h)
127	
128	Cg⊆ker h R⊆k = Cg-least (kercon h) R⊆k
129	```
130	
131	
132	##### Lifting and lowering of homs
133	
134	This section establishes that the operations of lifting and lowering of a setoid
135	algebra are homomorphisms.
136	
137	```agda
